    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersFagin's toasting fork sausagesPan-fried pork sausages on buttered toast with slow-cooked sticky onions and brown sauceHow to make it8 thick pork sausages2 tbsp vegetable oil3 brown onions, thinly sliced1 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp malt vinegar4 thick slices of crusty white bread30g butter80g brown sauce1/2 tsp saltCook the onions slowly in 1 tbsp of the oil with the salt for 20 minutes until soft and golden, then stir in the brown sugar and vinegar and cook 5 minutes more until sticky.Fry the sausages in the rest of the oil in another pan over medium heat, turning, until browned and cooked through.Toast the bread and butter it.Pile the onions and sausages on the toast and serve with brown sauce.Mr Brownlow's breakfast crumpetsHomemade griddled crumpets with salted butter, golden syrup and a sprinkle of cinnamon sugarHow to make it300ml milk7g dried yeast1 tbsp sugar300g plain flour1 tsp salt1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda80g salted butter80ml golden syrup1 tsp ground cinnamonWarm the milk with 100ml water, whisk in the yeast and 1 tsp of the sugar and leave until frothy.Beat into the flour and salt to a thick, smooth batter, cover and leave until sparkling apple.Whisk in the bicarb soda dissolved in 2 tbsp warm water.Grease 4 egg rings and a heavy pan with a little of the butter and cook the batter in the rings over low to medium heat until set and full of holes, then flip briefly. Repeat.Mix the rest of the sugar with the cinnamon and serve the crumpets hot with butter, golden syrup and cinnamon sugar.Pease pudding and saveloysStraight from Food, Glorious Food. Please, sir.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsWorkhouse governors' roast chicken and bread sauceLemon and thyme roast chicken with roast potatoes and carrots, peas and a creamy clove and nutmeg bread sauceHow to make it1.8kg whole chicken60g butter, softened1 lemon, halved4 sprigs of thyme1kg potatoes, peeled and halved500g carrots, in chunks3 tbsp olive oil2 tsp salt1 tsp ground black pepper500ml milk1 small brown onion, halved and studded with 4 cloves1 bay leaf100g fresh white breadcrumbs1 pinch of ground nutmeg300g frozen peasHeat the oven to 200°C. Rub the chicken with the butter and half the salt and pepper, push the lemon and thyme into the cavity and sit it in a roasting dish.Roast the chicken, adding the potatoes and carrots tossed with the oil and the rest of the salt and pepper for the last hour.Warm the milk with the studded onion and bay leaf, leave to infuse 20 minutes, then remove them and stir in the breadcrumbs and nutmeg. Simmer gently until thick.Rest the chicken 15 minutes, cook the peas and serve with the vegetables and bread sauce.Three Cripples pie and mashNancy leading Oom-Pah-Pah round the tables at the Three CripplesHow to make it700g beef chuck, diced2 tbsp plain flour2 tbsp vegetable oil2 brown onions500ml beef stock1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce2 sheets of shortcrust pastry1 sheet puff pastry1 egg1kg potatoes60g butter250ml milk1 parsley1 tbsp malt vinegarToss the beef in 1 tbsp of the flour and brown in the oil. Add the sliced onions for 5 minutes.Add the stock and Worcestershire, cover and simmer for 1 and a half hours until tender and thick. Cool.Line four pie tins with shortcrust, fill, top with puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.Boil the peeled potatoes for 20 minutes and mash with half the butter and a splash of the milk.Melt the rest of the butter, stir in the rest of the flour, whisk in the rest of the milk and simmer for 3 minutes, then blend with the parsley and vinegar for the liquor.Serve each pie with a scoop of mash and the liquor poured over.SweetsWorkhouse porridge bruleeCreamy vanilla and cinnamon oat pudding over stewed apples, with a crackling burnt sugar topHow to make it3 apples, peeled and diced2 tbsp brown sugar1 pinch of ground cinnamon100g rolled oats600ml milk150ml thickened cream2 tbsp sugar1 tsp vanilla extract1 pinch of salt4 tbsp caster sugarSimmer the apples with the brown sugar, cinnamon and 2 tbsp water until soft and split between 4 heatproof bowls.Simmer the oats with the milk, cream, sugar, vanilla and salt, stirring, until thick and creamy.Spoon over the apples, smooth the tops and leave to set.Scatter the caster sugar over the tops and burn with a blowtorch or under a very hot grill until glassy.DrinksArtful Dodger's hot ginger cordialFresh ginger, lemon, honey and cinnamon simmered into a cordial, lengthened with hot apple juice, in mugsHow to make it60g fresh ginger, sliced3 lemons, 2 juiced and peeled, 1 sliced80g honey1 cinnamon stick1 L apple juiceSimmer the ginger, lemon peel and juice, honey, cinnamon and 300ml water, then strain.Heat the apple juice until steaming and stir in the ginger cordial.Pour into 4 mugs and add a slice of lemon.
